assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a genuinely new window on the universe and answers the century-old cosmic-ray origin question. It is a discovery found in nature rather than inferred by theory, which is what I look for first. Strong existential and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept; Karle and Spiering are among the central builders and analysts of the detector and the collaboration. A fair three-person configuration looks possible, though a large-collaboration discovery always leaves some ambiguity about who was decisive. I would want the expert reports to weigh others in the founding group.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the 2013 diffuse-flux observation is confirmed over many years, and the 2017-2018 TXS 0506+056 coincidence and the Galactic-plane result add independent support. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether the decisive credit belongs to individuals outside the three names supplied, since only the supplied credited names may be proposed.
Origin of the bulk of the diffuse flux is still not fully identified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and then observing topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall state created a new classification of matter with broad influence on materials, transport and quantum devices. It combines a clear theoretical idea with decisive experimental confirmation, which is a combination I value.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 invariant; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. Hasan's ARPES observation of 3D topological insulators is also decisive, so the allocation among the four is the real difficulty and a three-person prize leaves out an important contribution.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation across many material platforms; recognition would be timely or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: How to split credit between the 2D quantum spin Hall work and the 3D topological insulator discovery, with other prominent theorists also absent from the credited names.
Practical applications remain limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the cosmic microwave background into a precision instrument, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the universe and cementing the Lambda-CDM picture with dark energy and dark matter. For a prize that I would explain with a cup of coffee, this is central, and it follows the CMB prizes already given.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission and Page was a principal instrument scientist; Spergel was the leading analyst of cosmological parameters. This is a plausible fair trio, though the mission team was large and the earlier COBE and later Planck results overlap in impact.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by Planck and other experiments; the 2003 first-year results are more than twenty years old, so recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees WMAP as sufficiently distinct from the COBE-recognized discovery and from Planck.
Persisting tensions such as the Hubble tension do not undermine the WMAP result itself but affect how the legacy is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of the shadows of M87* and Sgr A* provide direct visual evidence of black holes and a test of strong-field gravity, with a large conceptual and public impact, and a real existential dimension.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the VLBI development and the collaboration, and Narayan contributed key accretion-flow theory. This is a defensible trio, but the EHT is a collaboration of hundreds, so the credit is contested and the prize rules constrain it.
assessment.maturity: Results from 2019 and 2022 with polarization follow-ups are consistent with general relativity, but the independent confirmation is still limited to one collaboration's data and analysis, which makes me slightly cautious about timing.
uncertainties: Dependence on a single collaboration and image-reconstruction choices.
Large-collaboration credit and the roles of those not among the three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at the magic angle, and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene launched an entire field of moire matter. This is a prediction confirmed by experiment, with strong originality and a rapidly growing literature.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This is a clean three-person configuration. Other groups (e.g., Dean, Young, Yazdani) contributed to follow-ups but not clearly to the discovery.
assessment.maturity: Since 2018 there has been broad independent replication, though the superconducting mechanism remains unresolved; it is perhaps somewhat early but not premature.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is still debated.
Whether a longer track record is needed before recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and confirmed a mechanism in nature with enormous consequences. The theory was recognised in 2013, but the experimental discovery is a landmark result in its own right.
assessment.attribution: The discovery is a collaboration achievement of thousands. The supplied names are spokespersons and initiators, which captures leadership and construction rather than the decisive analysis; this is the weakest element in an otherwise very strong case.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independently observed by two experiments and the properties are well measured; recognition is long overdue under normal timing.
uncertainties: Prize rules and the unsuitability of an individual attribution to a large collaboration.
The committee may feel the 2013 prize already covered the Higgs discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a robust standard ruler for the expansion history and a direct handle on dark energy, a topic close to my own research. The 2005 detections in SDSS and 2dFGRS were decisive observational clues.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein et al. (SDSS) and Cole, Colless et al. (2dFGRS) made the two independent detections in 2005; the proposed trio reflects that but the theoretical origin of the idea is spread across several earlier theorists not listed.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, though the dark energy interpretation of recent data is still evolving.
uncertainties: Credit is shared with two surveys and earlier theory.
Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy are not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between light and artificial atoms possible on a chip and underlies superconducting quantum computing, an area of great current significance. It is a well-defined invention with a clear experimental demonstration.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed it theoretically, and Wallraff, together with Schoelkopf, demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. This is a natural, fair trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the technique, but the field's physics recognition may be partly covered by the recent 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so timing is less urgent.
uncertainties: Overlap with already recognised superconducting-circuit work.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for a clearer quantum computing milestone.
